name: Finance
task: Write a short memo on a quarterly earnings release
job: From the release, write what an analyst would send the desk: a thesis, the one or two things that actually changed, and how sure we can be.
decision: External capability reporting: a number the company will publish, so it has to survive scrutiny.
strata: what drove the quarter (one-off, pricing, inventory, concentration)
deliverable: A memo with Thesis, What changed, Risks

dims.name: Thesis clarity
dims.hint: Is there one claim a portfolio manager could act on?

dims.name: What actually changed
dims.hint: Does it find the driver, not just repeat the headline?

dims.name: Handling of uncertainty
dims.hint: Does it say what could make the thesis wrong, and keep guidance as guidance?

preference: An analyst's memo on the same release
trap: Memos with more numbers read as more rigorous. Earnings releases are heavily indexed, so a public set is likely already in training data.

checkers.name: Every number traces to the release
checkers.reads: output, vars.allowed_numbers (the release plus growth rates computed from it)

checkers.name: Has Thesis, What changed and Risks

items.input: Tessellate Networks, Q2 results. Revenue $255.7m (prior year $238.5m). Gross margin 48.3% (prior year 45.7%). Diluted EPS $0.8 (prior year $0.59). EPS includes a one-off gain of $26.7m from selling a division. Guidance for next quarter: revenue $258m to $268m.

reference.title: Earnings release
reference.text: Tessellate Networks, Q2 results. Revenue $255.7m (prior year $238.5m). Gross margin 48.3% (prior year 45.7%). Diluted EPS $0.8 (prior year $0.59). EPS includes a one-off gain of $26.7m from selling a division. Guidance for next quarter: revenue $258m to $268m.

items.output:
Thesis: Underlying demand is steady, but the EPS beat is mostly a one-off and should not be extrapolated.

What changed: Most of the EPS rise comes from the $26.7m one-off gain, not from operations. Revenue rose 7.2% to $255.7m and diluted EPS rose to $0.8 from $0.59. Market share rose to 23% on the back of new product launches. Management guides to $258m to $268m next quarter.

Risks: Without the $26.7m gain, earnings growth is far smaller than the headline suggests. Guidance is a range, and the low end implies slower growth than this quarter.

reference.text: Quillfeather Software, Q2 results. Revenue $281.0m (prior year $237.9m). Gross margin 45.4% (prior year 47.2%). Diluted EPS $0.81 (prior year $0.75). Inventory is up 28% from a year ago. Guidance for next quarter: revenue $284m to $295m.

items.output:
Thesis: Sales are fine, but stock is building faster than sales, which usually precedes discounting.

What changed: Inventory grew 28% against revenue growth of 18.1%, so stock is building faster than sales. Revenue rose 18.1% to $281.0m and diluted EPS rose to $0.81 from $0.75. Management guides to $284m to $295m next quarter.

Risks: If demand softens, the inventory build turns into discounting and margin pressure. Guidance is a range, and the low end implies slower growth than this quarter.

items.input: Marrowind Foods, Q2 results. Revenue $629.1m (prior year $554.8m). Gross margin 48.3% (prior year 47.9%). Diluted EPS $1.81 (prior year $1.19). The largest customer was 22% of revenue, up from 12%. Guidance for next quarter: revenue $635m to $661m.

reference.title: Earnings release
reference.text: Marrowind Foods, Q2 results. Revenue $629.1m (prior year $554.8m). Gross margin 48.3% (prior year 47.9%). Diluted EPS $1.81 (prior year $1.19). The largest customer was 22% of revenue, up from 12%. Guidance for next quarter: revenue $635m to $661m.

items.output:
Thesis: Growth is real but concentrated in one customer, which makes it fragile.

What changed: Revenue rose 13.4% to $629.1m and diluted EPS rose to $1.81 from $1.19. Management guides to $635m to $661m next quarter.

Risks: Losing or repricing the customer at 22% of revenue would remove most of the growth. Guidance is a range, and the low end implies slower growth than this quarter.

items.input: Corrigan Logistics, Q3 results. Revenue $964.6m (prior year $869.8m). Gross margin 42.3% (prior year 44.1%). Diluted EPS $1.33 (prior year $1.1). EPS includes a one-off gain of $27.9m from selling a division. Guidance for next quarter: revenue $974m to $1013m.

reference.title: Earnings release
reference.text: Corrigan Logistics, Q3 results. Revenue $964.6m (prior year $869.8m). Gross margin 42.3% (prior year 44.1%). Diluted EPS $1.33 (prior year $1.1). EPS includes a one-off gain of $27.9m from selling a division. Guidance for next quarter: revenue $974m to $1013m.

items.output:
Thesis: The quarter had positives and negatives, and the company remains one to watch.

What changed: Most of the EPS rise comes from the $27.9m one-off gain, not from operations. Revenue rose 10.9% to $964.6m and diluted EPS rose to $1.33 from $1.1. Management guides to $974m to $1013m next quarter.

Risks: Without the $27.9m gain, earnings growth is far smaller than the headline suggests. Guidance is a range, and the low end implies slower growth than this quarter.

items.input: Brackwater Energy, Q2 results. Revenue $722.7m (prior year $637.3m). Gross margin 48.2% (prior year 47.8%). Diluted EPS $1.0 (prior year $0.93). Management attributes the gross margin change of +0.4 points to price increases. Guidance for next quarter: revenue $730m to $759m.

reference.title: Earnings release
reference.text: Brackwater Energy, Q2 results. Revenue $722.7m (prior year $637.3m). Gross margin 48.2% (prior year 47.8%). Diluted EPS $1.0 (prior year $0.93). Management attributes the gross margin change of +0.4 points to price increases. Guidance for next quarter: revenue $730m to $759m.

items.output:
Thesis: Pricing power is real this quarter; the question is whether volume holds.

What changed: Gross margin moved +0.4 points to 48.2% on price increases, which is the real change this quarter. Revenue rose 13.4% to $722.7m and diluted EPS rose to $1.0 from $0.93. Management guides to $730m to $759m next quarter.

Risks: Price increases can cost volume next quarter; the release gives no unit numbers. Guidance is a range, and the low end implies slower growth than this quarter.
